brand._comment: The three senses of the vestibular system, and the brand's organising frame. Each pillar owns exactly two of ai_transformation.domains via the domain's `pillar` key — that mapping is the SSOT for the grouping rendered on index.html, ai-transformation.html and ai-readiness.html.

pillars.body: We design systems that reduce cognitive load, restore clarity, and stabilise the work environment so teams can think, breathe, and deliver.

pillars.tagline: How we feel our way forward
pillars.body: We don't celebrate busyness — we measure momentum. When your tools, rituals, and systems align, velocity becomes natural instead of forced.
We treat every challenge with weight and intention. No theatrics, no fluff — just grounded, evidence‑based design that pulls teams toward better outcomes.

agile.label: Agile Transformation
agile._comment: A maturity model: answers 'where are you now' and routes to a package.

stages.name: Foundational
stages.diagnostic_lens: Chaotic → tool sprawl, unclear workflows, burnout signals.
stages.focus: Restore clarity, reduce cognitive load, establish hygiene.
stages.outcomes: Reduced clutter, clear workflows, initial alignment.
stages.ai_augmentation: Automated Jira board cleanup, duplicate detection, backlog hygiene assistant.

stages.name: Emerging
stages.diagnostic_lens: Structured → boards cleaned, cadence exists, but ceremonies feel stale.
stages.outcomes: Improved trust, reduced burnout, meaningful rituals.
stages.deliverables: Morale metrics dashboard, role clarifications, team health interventions.
stages.ai_augmentation: Retro documentation, sprint flow insights, facilitation prompts.

price.proximity: Weekly on-site, ceremonies facilitated in person

stages.name: Enabled
stages.diagnostic_lens: Modular → frameworks adopted, backlog hygiene maintained, morale engagement rising.
stages.focus: Pilot modular Agile practices with one team, refine cadence, prepare for scale.
stages.outcomes: Autonomous teams, faster iteration, clear accountability.
stages.ai_augmentation: Backlog prioritization rubric, automated work item creation, sprint health dashboards.

price.proximity: Embedded 2 days/week with one pilot team

stages.name: Scaling
stages.diagnostic_lens: Sustainable (early) → teams self-manage hygiene, cross-team visibility emerging.
stages.focus: Replicate modular practices across teams, align governance.
stages.outcomes: Scalable Agile practices, consistent delivery, cross-team transparency.
stages.deliverables: Scaled rollout plan, cross-team coaching, governance map.
stages.ai_augmentation: Cross-team dashboards, compliance reporting, predictive bottleneck detection.

stages.name: Optimizing
stages.diagnostic_lens: Sustainable (advanced) → predictive dashboards, audit-ready compliance, continuous improvement culture.
stages.focus: Strategic agility, continuous improvement, business alignment.
stages.outcomes: Sustained momentum, strategic alignment, high morale.
stages.deliverables: Advanced dashboards, strategic workshops, compliance frameworks.
stages.ai_augmentation: Predictive analytics, strategic scenario modeling, continuous improvement dashboards.

diagnostic._comment: SSOT for the free self-assessment. The form fields AND the scoring script are both generated from this, so a question can never exist without a unique key.
diagnostic.intro: Six questions, about two minutes. You get a read on each dimension, not just one number.

dimensions.label: Tool hygiene
dimensions.question: Our tools and stack are consistently maintained and reliable.

dimensions.label: Team health
dimensions.question: Every team member contributes meaningfully during feedback opportunities.

dimensions.label: Enablement
dimensions.question: Our team has established routines that sustain flow and reduce friction.

dimensions.label: Governance
dimensions.question: Our team's cadence and conventions are aligned with other teams, enabling collaboration.

dimensions.label: Alignment
dimensions.question: Our work aligns with organisational goals, and outcomes are predictable.

dimensions.label: Adaptation
dimensions.question: We regularly reflect and adapt our practices to improve outcomes.

diagnostic._thresholds_comment: Cumulative score to stage. Six questions scored 1-5 gives a 6-30 range.

ai_transformation.label: AI Transformation
ai_transformation._comment: An engagement sequence: answers 'what happens when we work together'. Deliberately NOT a maturity model — the Agile practice owns that shape, and reusing its Declutter/Reboot/Enable vocabulary here would make the two practices indistinguishable.

ethos.name: Listen First
ethos.statement: We start from the assumption that your team already knows what is wrong. Our job is to surface it, not to arrive with the answer.
principles: The people doing the work hold the truth. Interviews, workshops and shadowing get it out; a template does not.
Validate before proposing. No premature optimisation, no solution looking for a problem.
Every finding is traceable to a person, a system, or a number — never to an assumption.

domains.name: Company Goals
domains.purpose: Understand what the organisation is actually trying to achieve — and whether its parts agree.
points: Gather and validate goals across execs, ops, product, and field teams
Test that goals are aligned, measurable, and sequenced — not merely stated
Map goals to AI leverage points, system dependencies, and capability gaps

domains.name: Systems
domains.purpose: Establish what you run, how well you run it, and what it is capable of.
points: Inventory every system in use — core, satellite, and shadow IT
Mastery: assess whether each system is used to a fraction of its potential
Integration: identify what can, should, and already does connect
AI-readiness: evaluate data quality, accessibility, and automation potential

domains.name: Pain Points
domains.purpose: Find where the pressure is greatest and put a number on it.
points: Locate bottlenecks, delays, rework, and compliance exposure
Map who and what is at risk — roles, customers, revenue, safety, reputation
Quantify impact in cycle time, cost, error rate, and emotional load

domains.name: Morale & Team Health
domains.purpose: Treat team health as a measurable input to the redesign, not a soft afterthought.
points: Team Health Reports measuring wellbeing, clarity, alignment, and psychological safety
Identify role misalignment — where responsibility and job description have parted ways
Surface the cultural blockers to transformation: fear, fatigue, confusion, siloing

domains.name: Roles & Alignment
domains.purpose: Put the right people in the right place for the operating model you are building toward.
points: Match capability, temperament, and workload to role
Redefine roles for an AI-enabled operating model
Clarify decision rights, ownership, and accountability

domains.name: AI Fit
domains.purpose: Decide where AI genuinely earns its place, rather than where it is fashionable.
points: Identify where AI meets a real need: automation, prediction, decision support, workflow augmentation
Prioritise opportunities by value, feasibility, and risk
Build AI literacy across teams so adoption is not left to chance

domains.name: Data Readiness
domains.purpose: Prepare the ground, so a system can rely on what you already hold.
points: Define AI-ready requirements: data, model behaviour, integration points
Resolve identity: one identifier per customer, job or product across systems
Establish what history exists, how clean it is, and what it can support

domains.name: Load & Capacity
domains.purpose: Read how much strain the work is carrying, because that is where AI has the most to hand back.
points: Measure sustained load against real capacity, team by team
Establish what actually happens when someone says they are at their limit
Target the heaviest and most repetitive load first — the largest recoverable hours

readiness._comment: SSOT for the AI transformation readiness radar. One axis per discovery domain, in the same order as domains above, so the chart is a map of the engagement rather than a slice of it. TWO VANTAGES per axis, not two indicators: "stated" is the respondent's read of what the organisation claims, "lived" is what they have witnessed from their own seat. They are NOT expected to agree — the divergence is the reading, and because both come from the same person on the same scale, wording severity and scale-use habits cancel between them. ⛔ DO NOT AVERAGE A PAIR: the mean of an espoused claim and a witnessed one describes neither, which is the fault the axis mean was reshaped to avoid. Keys are construct + vantage, never positional — a positional key meant three different things in one day during the September reshapes and had already been sent to the server in enquiry payloads. Deliberately NO stages and NO thresholds. See docs/READINESS_INSTRUMENT.md.
readiness.intro: Sixteen questions, about four minutes. There is no score and no stage — you get two readings of each of the eight areas we look at, what this organisation claims and what you have seen, and the widest distance between them.

questions.text: As far as I can tell, the goals here are measurable and sequenced, not merely stated.
The last time I had to choose between two things this organisation wanted, I knew which one it actually wanted.
questions.escape: Two priorities of mine have not collided

questions.text: The systems we own would do what we need, if we used them properly.
The last thing I needed to get done, I did in our systems rather than falling back to a spreadsheet.
We can put numbers on where the pressure is greatest.
The thing that wastes most of my week is something this organisation knows about.
People here can challenge an idea, even one from the person sponsoring it, without negative consequence.
The last time I disagreed with someone senior about how work should be done, it cost me nothing.
questions.escape: I have not disagreed with someone senior

questions.text: It is clear who decides what.
What I actually spend my week doing is what my job description says I do.
We can name specific places AI would meet a real need, not just where it is fashionable.
The work that takes most of my week is the same thing over and over.
The data here is trusted enough to run on.
The last time I needed a number, I got it from a system rather than by asking a person.
The last time I was near my limit, saying so changed something.
questions.escape: I have not been near my limit

phases.name: Listen
phases.blurb: Before anything is designed, the ground truth is established with the people who hold it.

steps.name: Establish the goals
steps.detail: Gather and validate what the organisation is trying to achieve, across every level that has a stake in it.

steps.name: Surface the ground truth
steps.detail: Interviews, workshops, and shadowing to extract the tacit knowledge that never reaches a status report.

steps.name: Map the systems
steps.detail: Every system in use, how well it is used, what it integrates with, and whether its data is fit for AI.

steps.name: Locate and quantify the pain
steps.detail: Where the pressure is greatest, who carries it, and what it costs in time, money, error, and morale.

steps.name: Assess people and roles
steps.detail: Team Health Reports and role-alignment analysis, feeding the redesign as measured input rather than opinion.

phases.name: Design
phases.blurb: Only once the picture is real do we design against it — value case first, so the work is justified before it is scoped.

steps.name: Identify AI opportunities
steps.detail: Find the leverage points where AI materially improves margin, throughput, or risk — and rule out the ones where it does not.

steps.name: Model the value case
steps.detail: Quantify the uplift and build the business case. This comes early because it is what unlocks the budget, not what reports on it afterwards.

steps.name: Redesign the operating model
steps.detail: Rebuild processes end to end with automation, agents, and predictive systems embedded — not bolted on.

steps.name: Define requirements and governance
steps.detail: Translate business need into AI-ready requirements, with regulatory, ethical, and operational boundaries set at the same time.

phases.name: Land
phases.blurb: A transformation that is designed but not adopted has changed nothing.

steps.name: Build the roadmap
steps.detail: Phases, dependencies, quick wins, and long-term uplift — the artefact an executive can actually hold and fund.

steps.name: Orchestrate delivery and adoption
steps.detail: Coordinate execs, product, engineering, ops, and compliance. Manage resistance and build confidence in the new workflows.

steps.name: Measure uplift and iterate
steps.detail: Track the value actually realised against the case that was modelled, then expand capability from what worked.

proof._comment: The case-study content. No customer names, no revenue figures — per founder direction. Claims here must stay true to what the platform actually does; this page is the practice's credibility and an overstatement here costs more than it wins.
proof.headline: We ran this playbook on ourselves.
proof.summary: Before advising anyone on AI transformation, we built and shipped one: a production system that drafts regulatory compliance documents for Australian road worksites, in a domain where a confident wrong answer is a safety problem rather than an embarrassment.
context: Traffic Management Plans and Traffic Guidance Schemes are the documents that govern how a road worksite is signed, staged and made safe. They are prepared by qualified people, audited by road authorities, and wrong details have physical consequences.
The rules are layered: a national baseline, then state and territory overlays that diverge from it. What is compliant in one jurisdiction is not automatically compliant in the next.

The work was slow, repetitive, and highly susceptible to transcription error — the profile that looks like an obvious AI candidate right up until you consider what happens when the model is confidently wrong.

principles.name: Never invent a safety-relevant value
principles.detail: When the system cannot find a value in the source document, it records it as absent. It does not estimate, interpolate, or fall back on what is usually true. A plausible-but-wrong number is worse than a blank field, because a blank field gets checked and a plausible number does not.

principles.name: Measure on two axes, never merge them
principles.detail: How much the system found, and how compliant the document is, are scored separately and never combined into one flattering number. The compliance scorer never sees whether a field was found, so it cannot reward the system for its own coverage. One blended metric would have hidden exactly the failure we most needed to see.

principles.name: Corroborate to demote, never to overwrite
principles.detail: When another data source agrees or disagrees with a value a qualified engineer confirmed, it adjusts our confidence in that value. It never silently replaces it. The human's judgement is the record; the machine annotates it.

principles.name: Calibration is the metric, not coverage
principles.detail: The question is not how much the system extracts. It is whether the things it says confidently are actually right. A tool that is right 70% of the time and honest about which 70% is far more useful than one that is right 90% of the time and cannot tell you which 10% to check.

principles.name: The qualified human is a design feature
principles.detail: The system is a drafting aid with a professional backstop, and it was designed that way from the start rather than retrofitted after a scare. That framing changes what you build, what you measure, and what you are willing to ship.

lessons.name: The pilot is not the hard part
lessons.detail: Getting a model to produce a plausible draft took a fraction of the effort. Everything after that — grounding it in the actual regulations, handling jurisdictional divergence, deciding what the system must refuse to answer — was the real work, and it is the part most AI programmes never reach.

lessons.name: Measure before you believe
lessons.detail: Every number we report is derived from a run we can point at, and every guard is driven over a known-bad input to prove it can actually fail. A check that has never failed is indistinguishable from a check that cannot.

lessons.name: Regulated domains reward restraint
lessons.detail: The features we chose not to automate did more for adoption than the ones we did. Professionals trust a tool that visibly knows its own limits, and refuse one that has been caught guessing even once.

proof.bridge: This is the same sequence the AI Transformation practice runs with clients: listen first, ground every claim in something measurable, design for the human who has to sign their name to the output, and be honest about where AI does not belong.
